repos/kacxx/aside-jot/issues/95.title: Skill: offer an aside add for open follow-ups when closing a jot
repos/kacxx/aside-jot/issues/95.body:
Path: ready — all questions decided (grill, 2026-10-14)

**Problem:** when "update jot N" finds the jot done but leaves work behind, that work ends up only in the `done --note`. The jot then leaves the inbox, and nothing brings the follow-up back.

Seen on a real inbox (2026-10-14): a jot asking for a staging test key was done, but the test the key was for was still blocked on access. The agent put the blocker in the suggested `--note` and told the user to type a new `>>` jot if they wanted a reminder. It can't create jots itself, by design.

Facts (checked 2026-10-14):
- `aside add` records the folder it is run from (`Cwd`, with its repo and branch) and has no flag to copy another jot's session or metadata (`cmd/aside/main.go`).
- `aside add` reads the text from stdin when given no arguments.
- Jots from `aside add` have no session, so `sessions` leaves them out; `find` lists them under "Not in a session" (`not_in_a_session` over MCP). Corrected 2026-10-15; see the fact-check in `docs/proposals/follow-up-jots.md`.
- The skill already says to offer `aside add` rather than run it ("Things to leave to the user", `skills/aside/SKILL.md`).
- `done --note` text is searchable, so the evidence stays findable after a jot closes.
- A BOM is stripped only when reading config files (`internal/setup/config.go`), not from `aside add`'s stdin. #80 left "the BOM from a PowerShell pipe into `aside add`" for later; it was reported in the Windows results on #77.

**Idea:** in the skill's "Updating a jot" routine, when the records show open work that isn't already tracked elsewhere, offer a ready-made follow-up command next to the `aside done` line. The user approves both, as with `done`. The agent still never runs `aside add` itself.

## Decisions

### D1: When to offer a follow-up

The agent offers a follow-up only when the records show open work that nothing else tracks (no Jira ticket, PR or other open jot covers it). A follow-up that duplicates a ticket is just more inbox noise.

### D2: Partly done jots

When the work is partly done, the agent offers both keeping the jot open and closing it with a follow-up, and the user picks.

### D3: Follow-up wording

The text reads `follow-up to #<id>: <the open work>`, written by the agent in its own words. Naming the source jot keeps the link to the session through `aside show <id>`. Own words keep it short and stop transcript text from being copied into a command.

### D4: Safe command form

The offered command passes the text through stdin with a quoted heredoc, not as an argument:

```
/full/path/to/aside add <<'EOF'
follow-up to #29: <the open work>
EOF
```

Inside `<<'EOF'` nothing expands, so running the command can't execute anything hidden in the text.

### D5: `aside add --from <id>`

Not tracked for now. Naming the jot (D3) is enough until there's evidence the missing session link matters.

### D6: Command order and note

The `aside add` line comes before the `aside done` line, and the done note ends in "; follow-up added as a new jot". Adding first means the follow-up exists before the original leaves the inbox.

### D7: "Update all"

Each follow-up line sits under its jot's done line and doesn't count toward the 10-session limit. The limit is about reading transcripts, and a follow-up costs no extra reads.

### D8: Run from the original repo

The offered command first `cd`s to the source jot's repo root (from `aside show <id>`), so the follow-up is listed under the same repo. It is left out if that folder no longer exists. Otherwise the follow-up records whatever folder the user runs it from.

### D9: Windows command form

On Windows, the agent offers a single-quoted here-string piped into aside instead of a heredoc:

```powershell
@'
follow-up to #29: <the open work>
'@ | & 'C:\path\to\aside.exe' add
```

A single-quoted here-string expands nothing, as with D4. This issue also includes the CLI fix that strips a leading BOM from `aside add`'s stdin, so Windows follow-ups don't start with a stray character.

## Open questions

None.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] "Updating a jot" offers an `aside add` follow-up only when the records show open work that nothing else tracks (D1).
- [ ] For partly done work, the agent offers both keeping the jot open and closing it with a follow-up (D2).
- [ ] The follow-up text reads `follow-up to #<id>: <the open work>`, in the agent's own words (D3).
- [ ] The follow-up command passes the text through a quoted heredoc on macOS and Linux (D4), and a single-quoted here-string piped into `aside.exe add` on Windows (D9).
- [ ] The command `cd`s to the source jot's repo root when that folder still exists (D8).
- [ ] The `aside add` line comes before the `aside done` line, and the done note ends in "; follow-up added as a new jot" (D6).
- [ ] "Updating all jots" puts each follow-up line under its jot's done line, outside the 10-session limit (D7).
- [ ] `aside add` strips a leading BOM from stdin, with a test (D9).
- [ ] The skill still says the agent never runs `aside add` itself.

**Scope:** `skills/aside/SKILL.md` ("Updating a jot" step 5, and the matching line in "Updating all jots"), plus the BOM strip on `aside add`'s stdin in `cmd/aside/main.go`. No MCP server change.

repos/kacxx/aside-jot/issues/95/comments.body:
Review of #95 and its tickets #97, #98 and #99, checked against main at `fe031d2`.

The design holds up. The tickets cover D1 to D9 with nothing dropped (D5 is deliberately untracked), and the quoted heredoc and single-quoted here-string close the injection hole for the new `add` line.

**Should fix before #97 is picked up**

1. **`add` and `done` can run independently.** If the `cd` or `aside add` fails, a user pasting the block still runs `aside done`, and the original closes with "follow-up added as a new jot" when it wasn't. That defeats D6. Chain them so `done` only runs if `add` succeeded, with the `&&` on the heredoc's first line:
   ```
   cd '<root>' && /path/aside add <<'EOF' && /path/aside done 29 --note "..."
   follow-up to #29: <the open work>
   EOF
   ```
   Windows PowerShell 5.1 has no `&&`, so #98 needs an `$LASTEXITCODE` check instead.
2. **#99 has no "partly done" verdict.** Step 3 has three verdicts (done, no sign yet, can't tell), and step 5 only fires for "done". D2 needs a fourth verdict, or a rule inside "done", and "Updating all jots" needs the same wording.
3. **The `done --note "<evidence>"` double-quote exposure is unfiled.** The proposal's Risks section says it deserves its own issue. Evidence comes from the transcript, so a `$(...)` in it would run when the line is pasted. #97 makes that line more prominent, so either file the issue or add one acceptance criterion to #97.

**Worth deciding**

4. Follow-up jots can never be status-checked (the cost of D5): `aside add` jots have no session, so "update all" will always say "can't tell" for them. The skill could read `activity` for the original jot `#N` when a jot starts `follow-up to #N:`.
5. D1 asks the agent to confirm nothing else tracks the work, but the skill gives no way to check. One sentence in step 5 (`search` the inbox) would do.
6. Use a subshell, `(cd '<root>' && ...)`, so the user's shell isn't left in another folder, and `Push-Location`/`Pop-Location` on Windows.
7. The rule "path ends in `.exe` or starts with a drive letter means PowerShell form" misfires for Git Bash or WSL users.
8. #98 says PowerShell 5.1 pipes ASCII, which emits no BOM, yet the BOM was seen in the #77 results. Name the shell and encoding that produced it, and add a test for stdin that is only a BOM.

**Small points**

- The skill reads MCP `show` first, but D8 says "the `root:` line of `aside show`" (CLI output). The skill should name both forms.
- This issue's fact list still says `find` leaves out `aside add` jots. The proposal's fact-check corrected that (`find` lists them under "Not in a session").
- The BOM strip in #98 doesn't depend on #97 and could ship first.

repos/kacxx/aside-jot/issues/95/sub_issu.title: Offer a follow-up jot when closing a jot (macOS and Linux)
repos/kacxx/aside-jot/issues/95/sub_issu.body:
Implements: D1, D3, D4, D6, D8, D10, D13, D14 — docs/proposals/follow-up-jots.md
Blocked by: None (can start immediately)
Parent: #95

## What to build

When "update jot N" finds a jot done but the records show open work that nothing else tracks, the agent offers a ready-made follow-up command next to the `aside done` line. Before offering it, the agent searches the inbox for the open work and checks the records for a ticket or PR that already covers it. The user runs the command, and a new jot reading `follow-up to #N: <the open work>` appears in the inbox, listed under the same repo as the original, before the original closes.

The offered command is one chain: it changes into the source jot's repo root, adds the follow-up through a quoted heredoc on stdin (so nothing in the text can expand or run), and only if that succeeded, closes the original with a note ending "; follow-up added as a new jot". If the folder change or the add fails, the original stays open. The agent writes the follow-up in its own words and still never runs `aside add` itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Before offering a follow-up, the agent searches the inbox for the open work and checks the records for a ticket or PR that covers it (D13).
- [ ] A follow-up is offered only when the records show open work that nothing else tracks (D1).
- [ ] The follow-up text reads `follow-up to #<id>: <the open work>`, in the agent's own words, not copied from the transcript (D3).
- [ ] The text goes through stdin with a quoted heredoc (`<<'EOF'`), not as an argument (D4).
- [ ] The add comes before the done, and the done note ends in "; follow-up added as a new jot" (D6).
- [ ] The done runs only if the add succeeded: one `&&` chain, with the `&&` on the heredoc's first line (D10).
- [ ] The command first changes into the repo root (the `root:` line of `aside show <id>`, or `repo_root` from the MCP `show` tool); that step is left out when the jot has no repo root, the folder no longer exists, or the root contains a single quote (D8).
- [ ] No subshell around the command (D14).
- [ ] Both commands use the full path to aside from the tool descriptions.
- [ ] The skill still says the agent never runs `aside add` itself.
- [ ] Verified end to end: running the offered command from another folder creates the follow-up under the original jot's repo, then closes the original; with a failing add, the original stays open.

repos/kacxx/aside-jot/issues/95/sub_issu.title: Windows follow-up form
repos/kacxx/aside-jot/issues/95/sub_issu.body:
Implements: D9, D10, D15 — docs/proposals/follow-up-jots.md
Blocked by: #97
Parent: #95

## What to build

On Windows, the follow-up offer from #97 works the same way in PowerShell. When the full path to aside ends in `.exe` or starts with a drive letter, the agent offers the Windows form instead of the heredoc. It changes location to the source jot's repo root literally (so folders with brackets work), pipes a single-quoted here-string into `aside.exe add` (nothing in it expands), and runs `aside.exe done` with the same note only if the add succeeded.

The follow-up text is plain ASCII. What Windows PowerShell 5.1 sends to a native program depends on the user's `$OutputEncoding`: the default is ASCII, which turns other characters into `?`, and other settings can add a byte order mark. ASCII text arrives intact either way. The byte order mark fix itself is #102.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The agent picks the Windows form when aside's path ends in `.exe` or starts with a drive letter, and the heredoc form otherwise (D15).
- [ ] The Windows form changes location with `Set-Location -LiteralPath`, left out under the same conditions as on macOS (no repo root, folder gone, root contains a single quote).
- [ ] The follow-up goes through a single-quoted here-string piped into `aside.exe add`, before the done (D9).
- [ ] The done is wrapped in `if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { … }`, so it runs only if the add succeeded (D10).
- [ ] The skill tells the agent to keep Windows follow-up text ASCII (no curly quotes or em dashes).

repos/kacxx/aside-jot/issues/95/sub_issu.title: Follow-ups for partly done jots and in "Update all"
repos/kacxx/aside-jot/issues/95/sub_issu.body:
Implements: D2, D7, D11, D12 — docs/proposals/follow-up-jots.md
Blocked by: #97
Parent: #95

## What to build

The follow-up offer from #97 extends to the cases it doesn't cover.

The skill gets a fourth verdict, "partly done", next to done, no sign yet and can't tell. For a partly done jot, the agent gives the user two choices: keep the jot open, or close it and add a follow-up for what's left. The user picks one.

In "Updating all jots", the same verdict is used. Each follow-up line sits directly under its jot's done line, so the user can run the pair or skip both. Follow-ups don't count toward the 10-session limit, because they cost no extra transcript reads. The routine says that follow-up jots themselves are left out, because they have no session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] "Updating a jot" and "Updating all jots" both have the "partly done" verdict (D11).
- [ ] For a partly done jot, the agent offers both keeping it open and closing it with a follow-up (D2).
- [ ] In "Updating all jots", each follow-up line appears under its own jot's done line, not merged with others (D7).
- [ ] Follow-ups don't count toward the 10-session limit (D7).
- [ ] "Updating all jots" says follow-up jots are left out because they have no session (D12).
- [ ] The agent still runs none of the offered commands itself.

repos/kacxx/aside-jot/pulls?state=closed.body:
Refs #95

Adds decisions D10 to D15 to `docs/proposals/follow-up-jots.md`, from a second grill on the review comment on #95. D1 to D9 are unchanged and the Status stays **decided**.

- **D10:** `done` runs only if `add` succeeded (`&&` chain on macOS and Linux, `$LASTEXITCODE` check on Windows).
- **D11:** a fourth verdict, "partly done", in both routines.
- **D12:** no status checks for follow-up jots for now; the skill says they're left out of "Updating all jots".
- **D13:** before offering a follow-up, search the inbox and check the records for a ticket or PR.
- **D14:** no subshell.
- **D15:** the command form still follows aside's path; Git Bash listed as a risk.

Also:
- Shape: the chained macOS command, the Windows `$LASTEXITCODE` check, both forms of `show` (`root:` on the CLI, `repo_root` over MCP), and a test for stdin that is only a BOM. The BOM fix is marked as able to ship first.
- Fact-check: the PowerShell 5.1 encoding row now explains the BOM seen on #77 (that session wasn't on the default `$OutputEncoding`). New rows for the chained heredoc (probed in zsh and bash), empty stdin, and the MCP `repo_root` field.
- Risks: Git Bash, `Set-Location` failing, and the non-ASCII risk reworded to depend on `$OutputEncoding`.

After this merges, #97, #98 and #99 get updated for the new decisions.
